claims.text: Integrating machine-learning models with first-principles calculations can improve determination of transition temperature in multicomponent high-entropy materials.
Integrating machine-learning models with first-principles calculations can improve determination of fusion enthalpy and entropy in multicomponent high-entropy materials.
Integrating machine-learning models with first-principles calculations can improve determination of volume change at the transition.
Integrating machine-learning models with first-principles calculations can improve determination of dense-fluid heat capacity.
Machine learning can efficiently screen the large compositional spaces of multicomponent high-entropy materials.
Machine learning can identify patterns in thermodynamic properties.
First-principles calculations can provide accurate predictions of transition temperatures.
First-principles calculations can accurately predict relevant material properties in high-entropy alloys.
A first-principles-based high-throughput approach can screen thousands of AlCoCrFeNi compositions with accuracy comparable to established first-principles methods and with greater efficiency.
The proposed integration will improve both accuracy and efficiency relative to experiments, DFT free-energy studies, and TOR-TILD.
Phase diagrams and thermodynamic properties act as the structural mediator between the intervention and improved transition-property determination.
The proposed approach is limited to high-temperature states and multicomponent systems.
Machine-learning accuracy depends on the quality of the training data.
Integrating machine learning with first-principles calculations may still require significant computational resources.
